title: Messe Stuttgart Announces Winners of the Quantum Effects Award 2026 Across Four Hardware and Software Categories - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Messe Stuttgart's Quantum Effects Award 2026 went to four TRL 5+ projects with commercial pathways: C12/Thales QuantumTrack (carbon-nanotube spin-cQED annealing for radar tracking), Fraunhofer FOKUS's open-source Eclipse Qrisp, QSENSATO's chip-scale OPM array CODA, and PicoQuant's 64+ channel HydraHarp 500 L time-tagger for QKD networks.

insights.claim: The Quantum Effects Award 2026 jury only evaluated submissions at Technology Readiness Level 5 or higher across hardware, software, sensing and networking, favoring projects with direct industry utility and commercial deployment pathways.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: European industry juries are rewarding near-deployment quantum products rather than lab science, signaling where commercial attention is shifting.
insights.quote: Evaluating submissions at Technology Readiness Level 5 (TRL 5) or higher across hardware, software, sensing, and networking
insights.locator: The jury for the international Quantum

insights.claim: C12 and Thales won the hardware category for QuantumTrack, which maps Multiple Hypothesis Tracking radar data association onto a carbon nanotube spin-cQED annealing architecture, solving Maximum Weighted Independent Set problems with ~50 ms target latency.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A defense prime (Thales) co-developing a real-time radar use case gives C12's carbon-nanotube spin-qubit platform a concrete defense application narrative.
insights.quote: maps Multiple Hypothesis Tracking (MHT) radar data association onto a carbon nanotube spin circuit quantum electrodynamics (spin-cQED) annealing architecture

insights.claim: Fraunhofer FOKUS won the software award for Eclipse Qrisp, an open-source Python framework that translates high-level constructs like variables, functions and loops directly into gate-based circuits across heterogeneous backends.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hardware-independent open-source tooling backed by European institutions may commoditize parts of the quantum software layer that proprietary SDK vendors hope to monetize.
insights.locator: In the software category, Fraunhofer FOKUS

insights.claim: Italian spinoff QSENSATO SRL was recognized for CODA, an integrated atomic-photonic chip platform using laser-written alkali vapor cells to miniaturize optically pumped magnetometers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Miniaturized OPMs are a nearer-term commercial quantum sensing market (e.g. medical diagnostics, metrology) than quantum computing.
insights.locator: In sensing, Italian spinoff QSENSATO SRL

insights.claim: PicoQuant's HydraHarp 500 L time-tagger offers 64+ input channels, 1 ps resolution, 680 ps dead time and White Rabbit synchronization aimed at distributed QKD networks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Photon-counting instrumentation vendors are a picks-and-shovels play on quantum networking build-outs.
insights.quote: ultra-short dead time (680 ps), and White Rabbit timing synchronization for distributed QKD networks
insights.locator: In quantum networking, photonics vendor PicoQuant
